short: Vandals, Alans and Suebi crossed the Rhine unopposed, breaking a frontier Rome never fully restored.
full:
On the night of 31 December 406 CE, a mixed force of Hasding and Siling Vandals, Alans and Suebi crossed the Rhine near Mainz, with the middle Rhine garrison thinned by earlier withdrawals to fight the usurper Constantine III. Roman defences on the frontier, weakened for years, offered little resistance, and the invaders poured into Gaul largely unchecked.

The crossing opened years of pillaging across Gaul before the invaders pushed on into Spain by 409. Unlike earlier incursions, this frontier was never restored: the Vandals and Alans eventually crossed into Africa in the 420s, and the Rhine ceased to function as a defended limit of the empire. Prosper of Aquitaine's chronicle preserves the precise date, and later writers treated the crossing as the moment the western frontier system began to fail for good.
